findings.title: Active descendant no longer updates while Ctrl/Cmd is held during quick navigation
findings.body:
`!this.keyMods.ctrlCmd` blocks the `aria-activedescendant` update whenever Ctrl (Cmd on macOS) is held. Quick-navigate flows move focus through the list with the modifier held: repeated Ctrl+P in Quick Open, or Ctrl+Tab editor switching.

In those flows the attribute stays on the old item or stays removed, so screen readers announce nothing or the wrong item. That is a new accessibility regression. The same guard in the tree handler (line 262) has the same problem.

Fix: remove this guard and handle the Ctrl case in the keydown handler instead.

findings.title: Ctrl keydown still removes aria-activedescendant, so the reported announcement is not fixed
findings.body:
The issue says pressing Ctrl makes the screen reader announce the placeholder. The PR description blames the `onKeyDown` handler, which removes `aria-activedescendant` on every key, Ctrl included. This handler is unchanged here apart from the comment wording; it has no modifier-key guard.

Pressing Ctrl alone still drops the active descendant. Focus then falls back to the input, and the reader announces "Type the command to run". The new `ctrlCmd` checks on `onDidChangeFocus` do not help, because pressing Ctrl alone triggers no focus change.

Fix: skip the removal when `e.keyCode` is Ctrl, Shift, Alt or Meta, as the description says.

findings.title: New test asserts nothing (`assert.ok(true)`)
findings.body:
The test only sets the placeholder and then calls `assert.ok(true)`. It never checks the `aria-label` or whether redundant DOM writes are skipped, so it passes whatever the new dedup logic does.

Fix: assert the input element's `aria-label` after each change, or spy on `setAttribute` to verify that setting the same value does not write.
